newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech finmin takes over management of OB Invest.
newsitem.headline: Czech finmin takes over management of OB Invest.

text.p: The Czech Finance Ministry said on Tuesday that it would impose its forced administration on investment firm O.B. Invest, a unit Ceskoslovenska Obchodni Banka (CSOB), effective on Wednesday, because of repeated violations of financial laws.

"On the basis of an audit of this company (OB Invest) and its management of funds, profound and repeated violations of the law on investment companies and investment funds were found," the ministry said in a statement.
"The forced administration has a preventative character to limit the further possibility of damaging the interests or property of investors," it added.

It said violations were in connection with OB Invest's management of the funds Zlaty Investicni Fond Kvanto a.s., and Kvanto Investicni Privatizacni Fond a.s., breaking rules of trading in securities.

It said the violations were connected to buying shares of a company at an "overvalued price" and selling them at an "undervalued price", and conducting operations "having a character of forbidden lending which does not hold to lawfully permitted limits".
The statement did not elaborate and ministry officials were not immediately available for further comment.
The firm has 15 days to appeal the decision, the ministry said.
The ministry appointed Petr Kraus as OB Invest's administrator from its list of authorised officials.
